# Release Notes

> Latest product updates

## October 27, 2026

### Outbound traffic is IPv4 only

Gitar now reaches code hosts over IPv4 only. Every outbound request, including clones, pushes, webhook registration and code host API calls, leaves from the IPv4 addresses in [Network Access](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/network-access.md). An allowlist that holds those addresses needs no change.

If you allowed Gitar's IPv6 range, `2600:1f28:74:4000::/60`, remove it. Gitar keeps the range reserved for now, so it is not reissued while allowlists are updated, but it will be released later.

## October 16, 2026

### Cross-PR Analysis

Cross-PR dashboard with totals for open findings, PRs involved, and resolved findings above a finding that links two PRs

Gitar now checks related open PRs for changes that could break each other, within a repository or across connected repositories. For example, one PR might remove an API field that another still reads.

Findings carry a **cross-pr** label and link to the other PR. Browse them in **Dashboard -> [Cross-PR](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/cross-pr-analysis.md)**, labeled **Cross-MR** on GitLab. Cross-PR Analysis is on by default for Enterprise.

### Agentic Security

Agentic Security dashboard with totals for open critical and important findings, fixed findings, and affected repositories above the findings list

Agentic Security brings [Sonar's OpenAI Daybreak collaboration](https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/sonar-joins-openai-daybreak-program/) to Gitar. A change to an agent skill can remove a required approval step or leak credentials and private code. Gitar reviews the instructions and the scripts they call together to catch those risks.

Gitar catches a dropped sign-off step by comparing instruction versions. It inspects suspicious content without running it and validates each issue before posting a finding. Repository instructions cannot suppress these checks. Agentic Security is included with Enterprise.

Open **Dashboard -> [Agentic Security](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/agentic-security.md)** to browse critical and important security findings, with critical findings first. Select a count to see open or fixed findings, or repositories with open findings.

### Auto-apply criteria

Auto-apply review criteria card with the organization review criteria field and a note on extending it with .gitar/config/apply.md

[Auto-apply criteria](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-apply.md) limit which review findings Gitar may fix automatically. Set organization criteria in **Settings -> Configuration** and extend them per repository with `.gitar/config/apply.md`.

Auto-apply still requires per-PR opt-in, and explicit fix requests work as before. **Options** in the dashboard comment shows how many findings were fixed and why the rest were skipped.

### Verification in the dashboard comment

Dashboard comment with Verification below Code Review, showing badges for objectives, rules, and Broader impact

[Verification](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review.md#verification) brings rule results, linked issue objectives, Knowledge, and cross-repo checks into one section below **Code Review**. Badges such as `Objectives 18/18` or `Rules 4/4 met` show the results. A section opens by default only when a rule fails or an objective is uncovered.

Cross-repo and Cross-PR coverage are grouped under **Broader impact**, with links to the inspected repositories and PRs.

### AWS CodeCommit in preview

Gitar now reviews [AWS CodeCommit](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/aws-codecommit.md) PRs with inline findings and analyzes failed CodeBuild and CodePipeline runs. Reply `Gitar fix` to a finding to request a fix. When every failed pipeline action is unrelated to the PR, Gitar retries the stage.

Setup generates IAM steps for the selected AWS account, region, and access. Gitar manages EventBridge delivery. Enterprise organizations can request preview access. Auto-approve and merge blocking are unavailable during the preview.

### Concourse and Woodpecker CI analysis

Concourse connection dialog with server URL, local username, permitted teams, and a build URL used to check access

Woodpecker connection dialog with server URL and API token fields

Gitar now reads failed [Concourse](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-ci/concourse.md) and [Woodpecker](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-ci/woodpecker.md) steps and explains the failure on the PR. Connect either provider in **Settings -> Integrations**. Both support GitHub repositories, and Gitar checks build-log access before saving.

Woodpecker requires v3.19.0 with the GitHub forge. One organization can connect several Woodpecker servers.

### CI recovery after a Gitar push

[CI recovery](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/ci-failure-analysis.md#recovery-after-a-gitar-fix) is now available to every organization. When a Gitar commit breaks passing CI, Gitar pushes a follow-up fix, even with auto-apply off.

Recovery applies only when the failure is related to the PR. It stops after three consecutive Gitar commits, or when someone else pushes to the branch.

### Up to three configuration repositories

Organizations can now share configuration from up to three [configuration repositories](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/configuration-repository.md), selected in **Settings -> Configuration**. Local rules and skills take precedence. Among shared repositories, the first selected repository wins when rules or skills overlap.

Configuration repositories can also hold shared auto-approve, auto-merge and risk criteria that extend the organization baseline. Each repository's own files apply on top, and shared criteria do not turn automation on.

### Source citations in findings

When a finding depends on how an external API behaves, Gitar looks up the documentation and cites the source beside the claim. Reviewers can check the claim without searching for it.

### Drill-downs from dashboard counts

Counts on **Overview** and **Reviews** now open paginated lists of the underlying PRs and findings. Browse by category, repository, contributor, or processed PR. The lists keep the selected dates and link back to the code host.

### Usability improvements

* [Risk Triage](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/risk-triage.md) reasons name the possible harm, not only what the change does.
* Organization members can view the [Knowledge](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/knowledge.md) and [Cross-repo](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/cross-repo-analysis.md) dashboards. Marking knowledge stale and changing settings stay admin-only.
* Sort the Knowledge library by **Recently added** or **Recently used**. **Most used** is the default.
* Replying `please fix` or `gitar apply` to a finding with one suggested fix applies it, the same as checking its box.
* Test a saved [MCP server](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/custom-integrations.md) connection from settings. Gitar lists the server's tools without starting a review.
* The Cross-repo dashboard adds **Linked Repositories**, showing each repository's neighbors and the findings behind each link. Overview metrics open the matching findings.
* At organization scope, the **Overridden in N repositories** badge on a code review setting lists those repositories, with a reset to the organization default for each.
* [GitLab](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/gitlab.md) setup opens on group onboarding, where a top-level group covers the projects in its subgroups. Group search ranks exact path matches first.
* GitLab connections accept a personal access token from a dedicated user, as well as a service account token.
* [Functional validation](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/functional-validation.md) recognizes lowercase ticket keys and a key at the start of the PR title, such as `proj-123 Fix login`.

### Bug fixes

* GitLab inline comments on unchanged context lines are no longer dropped, and comments are no longer placed on a guessed line when the reviewed line is missing from the MR diff.
* Gitar's fix commits on GitLab use the connected account's commit email.
* GitHub inline comments that hit a temporary GitHub error are retried instead of lost.
* GitLab draft MRs respect the setting to skip drafts.
* Resolving a finding on GitLab resolves the whole discussion, including replies.
* Gitar no longer misses GitLab merge requests that are waiting on a security policy pipeline check.
* Fork PRs from a branch named like the default branch, such as `main`, are reviewed instead of skipped.
* PRs from private forks that Gitar cannot read check out from the upstream repository instead of failing.
* An invalid UTF-8 byte in legacy-encoded source no longer stops a review.
* Push-triggered reviews use the pushed commit, so findings from an older revision are no longer reposted.
* Inline threads resolve when their finding resolves, instead of at the end of the review.
* A finding closes as won't fix only when the author agrees it is correct and declines to fix it. An acknowledgement or a promised follow-up keeps it open.
* Turning merge blocking off dismisses the blocking review Gitar had already placed.
* On public repositories, functional validation reads only issues from the same repository, so content from trackers such as Jira or Linear is not quoted in public comments.
* Finding status changes made in the dashboard are no longer overwritten by a concurrent review update.
* Renamed repositories, and new repositories that reuse an old name, keep their own settings.
* Bitbucket reviews of PRs that target a custom branch no longer come back empty.
* Auto-approved Bitbucket PRs get one approval notice instead of two.
* Bitbucket processing statuses complete, and CI recovery works on Bitbucket.
* The Reviews dashboard shows Bitbucket authors' profiles.
* GitHub CI failures are no longer missed when the installation reaches its rate limit.
* Cross-repo coverage reports an incomplete inspection instead of zero impacts when a repository could not be read.
* The Overview findings chart shows an error with a retry option when loading fails, instead of zero.

## September 17, 2026

### Knowledge that learns from the team

Knowledge dashboard showing the library, source filters, and review usage

Gitar learns from review conversations and carries relevant guidance into later reviews, with citations back to its sources. Enterprise admins can now browse the library, inspect usage, and mark outdated entries stale in **Dashboard -> [Knowledge](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/knowledge.md)**.

### Cross-Repo Analysis is out of preview

Cross-repo dashboard showing repository connections and findings with their fix locations

Catch a change that breaks another repository before it lands. The new [Cross-repo dashboard](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/cross-repo-analysis.md) shows affected repositories and recurring problems, with findings that explain which side needs a fix. Available on Enterprise, with connections discovered automatically.

### Azure DevOps Server and Bitbucket Data Center are generally available

Azure DevOps connection dialog with the Server option selected

Bitbucket connection dialog with the Server option and app connection flow

[Azure DevOps Server](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/azure-devops-server.md) and [Bitbucket Data Center](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/bitbucket-data-center.md) are out of preview, joining the cloud integrations already out of beta. Connect from Gitar's settings to bring reviews and automated fixes to self-hosted repositories.

### Focus attention with Risk Triage

Example expanded Code Review with a risk assessment and review verdict

[Risk Triage](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/risk-triage.md) now assesses the whole PR as Low, Medium, or High risk, even when the review finds no defects. Define risk for the organization, add repository guidance, and use the result in approval and merge criteria. The assessment appears in the expanded Code Review section.

### Turn on automatic fixes with a label

Add [`gitar-managed`](https://docs.gitar.ai/labels#gitar-managed) to a GitHub PR or GitLab MR to enable automatic fixes for that change. Removing the label restores the configured default, and explicit per-PR settings still take precedence. Existing plan and usage limits apply.

Example gitar-managed label beside dashboard options showing auto-apply enabled

### Analyze Jenkins build failures

Jenkins connection dialog with username, API token, and server URL fields

Connect [Jenkins](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-ci/jenkins.md) to have Gitar read failing build logs and explain the failure on the pull request. When Jenkins exposes stage logs or JUnit results, Gitar uses those to narrow the analysis. No Gitar plugin is required in Jenkins.

### Connect YouTrack

YouTrack connection dialog with base URL and permanent token fields

Connect [YouTrack Cloud](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/youtrack.md) or a self-managed instance. Gitar reads linked issues and checks their requirements against the change. Rules can create follow-up issues or update existing ones.

### Connect multiple Azure DevOps instances

Manage multiple [Azure DevOps connections](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/azure-devops.md) in one Gitar organization, including cloud and Server instances. Each connection has its own credentials and project selection, so teams can work across instances from the same settings page.

### Choose between Focused and Thorough reviews

Enterprise teams can choose [review depth](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review.md#review-depth). **Focused** comments only where Gitar is confident the issue matters. **Thorough** includes smaller issues, with more comments to assess. Set the organization default in **Settings -> Configuration**, then override it per repository where needed.

Review depth settings showing Focused and Thorough, with Thorough selected

### Reviews understand stacked changes

On GitHub and GitLab, Gitar now receives [review context](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review.md) about open changes stacked after the one under review. It can account for work planned in a later PR when judging whether the current change is incomplete.

### Reuse existing agent instructions and skills

Gitar now reads [repository instructions](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/repository-config.md) from `.claude/rules` alongside `.cursor/rules` and discovers [skills](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/skills.md) in `.agents/skills`. Keep guidance and reusable skills in the locations the team's coding tools already use, including in the shared configuration repository.

### Clearer setup and feature documentation

The documentation now includes a [platform support matrix](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/platform-support.md), with corrected connection steps and less repeated guidance across feature pages. Check what each platform supports and follow the setup path for cloud or self-hosted repositories.

### Usability improvements

* Enterprise admins can enable Knowledge and Cross-repo independently from their dashboards. New Enterprise organizations get both enabled by default. Disabling either stops future processing and retains its history.
* The expanded Code Review section shows review coverage, so the scope of Gitar's investigation is visible beside its findings.
* GitLab setup checks webhook delivery, with setup guidance available from connection settings.
* Azure DevOps now honors [`gitar-skip`](https://docs.gitar.ai/labels#gitar-skip) for code review and rule evaluation.
* Manage Bitbucket Data Center repositories from the configuration page, including refreshing repository discovery and webhooks.
* Hover over category and repository tables in the [Reviews dashboard](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/insights.md) to see the breakdown behind each total.
* Rule results are grouped by their authored rule file, and the dashboard footer summarizes rules that did not apply.
* Filter [Gitar Activity](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/insights.md) by repository to focus Insights on the projects that matter.
* Refresh Bitbucket Cloud repositories on demand, and resume an interrupted connection flow without starting the installation again.
* Jenkins and YouTrack credentials are checked before they are saved.

### Bug fixes

* Approval decisions are re-evaluated after code or policy changes. A previous approval or rejection no longer survives after its supporting evidence changes.
* Findings targeted by a requested fix stay open when the fix cannot be pushed, preventing approval based on a change that never reached the branch.
* An incomplete review no longer produces an approval just because it recorded no findings.
* Rebases no longer bring unrelated upstream changes into the review diff.
* Applying a suggested fix preserves overlapping changes that the author already explained or asked Gitar to keep.
* Suggested fixes that are identical to the code they replace are no longer offered.
* GitHub review checks no longer remain stuck running after Gitar finishes.
* Resuming a comment conversation restores the current CI analysis instead of incorrectly reporting that no failures were detected.
* Buildkite and Bitrise failure events now reach CI analysis.
* Auto-merge reporting now reflects whether the platform accepted the request, including when Gitar pushed a fix during the review.
* Azure DevOps reviews now read changes beyond the first 100 files.
* GitLab merge-blocking detection checks the merge request's actual state, avoiding incorrect reports that a merge is blocked.
* Disconnecting an Azure DevOps, GitLab, or Bitbucket Data Center connection no longer cancels work on unrelated connections. Repository discovery also preserves disconnected Azure repositories.
* Bitbucket Data Center respects the setting to skip draft pull requests, and commits made through service-account connections are signed.
* Automatic fixes select the correct repository when multiple connections contain repositories with the same name.
* [LiteLLM connections](https://docs.gitar.ai/administration/bring-your-own-model.md) now use the gateway's configured model routing and credentials.
* Insights repository filters no longer fail when the selected repository list is too large for a URL.

## August 28, 2026

### Bring your own model

The AWS Bedrock option showing residency geography, role ARN, the global inference toggle, and the optional guardrail fields

Run every LLM call for your organization on your own account. Open **Settings -> Configuration -> Bring Your Own Model** and pick a provider: an Anthropic API key, an AWS Bedrock role, or a gateway you run through LiteLLM, Portkey, or OpenRouter.

Gitar still picks the model for each task. You pick the account those calls are served from and the region they run in.

Bedrock adds a residency geography, a cross-region inference toggle, and an optional guardrail that Gitar sends on every call, so PII masking you configured applies.

**Test connection** invokes each provider before saving, so a role that cannot reach a model fails at setup rather than on your next review. Enterprise plan. [Bring Your Own Model](https://docs.gitar.ai/administration/bring-your-own-model.md)

### Connect Harness and TeamCity

TeamCity integration form with the access token and server URL

Harness and TeamCity join Buildkite, CircleCI, and Bitrise as connectable CI providers. Give Gitar a token that can read builds, and it downloads the log for each failing build and analyzes it. See [Harness](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-ci/harness.md) and [TeamCity](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-ci/teamcity.md).

### Share skills, rules, and review instructions across repositories

Name one repository as your organization's configuration repository, and every other repository inherits its `.gitar/` directory: skills, rules, review instructions, and agent instructions.

A repository's own copy of a skill or rule wins over the inherited one, so a team can override a central default. Set the repository at the foot of the **Repositories** card in **Settings -> Configuration**. Pro and Enterprise plans, rolled out per organization. [Configuration Repository](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/configuration-repository.md)

Skills are new in this release too. A skill is a `SKILL.md` of instructions your rules or PR comments call by name, versioned with your code, and it can ship scripts for the agent to run. Gitar loads a skill into the calling agent's own turn with that agent's full toolset. [Skills](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/skills.md)

### Functional validation reads every issue source

A PR that links a GitHub issue, a GitLab issue, an Azure DevOps work item, a Bitbucket Cloud issue, or a Plane work item now gets the same **Implementation Status** block that Jira and Linear already had.

Gitar reads the issue, splits it into objectives, judges each one against the diff, and re-judges on every push. On a code host with its own tracker, `Fixes #123` is enough. Turn it off with the **Functional validation** toggle on the configuration page. Enterprise plan. [Functional Validation](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/functional-validation.md)

### Custom integrations are now MCP endpoints

Add MCP server dialog showing the endpoint field, the authentication selector, one auth header row, and one allowed tool

A custom integration is an https MCP server URL. Supply the endpoint, name the HTTP headers your credentials travel in, and list which tools the server may expose. [Custom Integrations (MCP)](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/custom-integrations.md)

### Track work in Plane

Plane connection dialog in Gitar settings, with fields for base URL, workspace slug, and API token

Plane joins Jira and Linear as a work item source, on Plane Cloud and on self-hosted instances. Gitar reads the work items a PR links, and your rules can have it search, create, update, comment on, and transition them. [Plane](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/plane.md)

### Choose which branches Gitar reviews

Scope settings with allowed and excluded target branch fields

Two scope settings, **Allowed target branches** and **Excluded target branches**, filter PRs by the branch they merge into. Both take names or globs such as `main` or `release/*`, and the exclude list wins.

Teams on a stacked branching model can put `main,release/*` in the allowed list to keep Gitar quiet on intermediate merges and review only the merge that matters. The filter applies on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps. [Target branch patterns](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/settings.md#target-branch-patterns)

### More platform coverage

Azure DevOps and Bitbucket are out of beta.

Self-hosted has guides of its own. [Azure DevOps Server](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/azure-devops-server.md) and [Bitbucket Data Center](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/bitbucket-data-center.md) cover the inbound reachability and webhook egress an on-premises server needs.

GitLab self-hosted Free edition is now supported. [GitLab](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/gitlab.md)

### Usability improvements

* Auto-merge takes criteria. Write your merge conditions in plain language and Gitar evaluates them in the same pass as auto-approve, or commit `.gitar/config/merge.md` to set a policy per repository. Require the per-repository file and a repository without one is never armed. [Auto-Merge](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-merge.md)
* The dashboard comment says why a PR was not armed for auto-merge, instead of leaving you to guess.
* Steer the prose Gitar writes under the Code Review header with **Review summary instructions** in settings. Leave it empty for the current default.
* Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center share one connect entry with **Cloud** and **Server** tabs, in settings and in onboarding, and the Connections card lists every connected Cloud workspace with a link to add another.
* Integration cards prefill their stored configuration when reopened and show which secrets are already set.
* Jira Cloud runs over the Gitar Forge app instead of 3LO OAuth, so Gitar can create, update, comment on, transition, and link issues while holding no Atlassian credential of its own. Existing installs need an admin to re-approve consent.
* On Azure DevOps, only the newest auto-approve notice survives, rather than one stacking per commit.
* The Confluence card lists which spaces the Gitar app can read, per site, and shows a distinct state when the app is installed but no space has been shared with it yet.
* A ticket key in the title position, such as `[ENG-1] Add pagination`, links to that ticket on its own, with no `Fixes` keyword needed.
* Enterprise organizations have an in-product support widget.
* Organization slugs that would collide with a Gitar route are rejected at create and rename, instead of returning 404 on every page in the organization.
* Community links point to the Sonar community rather than Discord.

### Bug fixes

* Gitar posts fewer, cleaner comments. The dashboard comment updates in place instead of reposting on every run, which was notifying everyone on a PR each time, and it stops rolling once a PR is closed or merged.
* Review output reads correctly. Findings are no longer cut off mid-code, code in a finding no longer breaks the formatting of the rest of the comment, and the summary can no longer claim a change introduced no regressions on a review that found nothing.
* Gitar is accurate about merge state. It no longer says a merge request is blocked when anyone could merge it.
* CI analysis stays current. A failure already fixed on an earlier commit is not reported again, and the analysis no longer disappears from the GitLab dashboard comment moments after it posts.
* Webhook delivery is correct on GitLab and Bitbucket. GitLab organizations no longer receive every event twice, a disconnected organization stops delivering, Bitbucket honors `skip_draft_prs`, and a busy Bitbucket repository no longer drops its own CI events.

Public repositories with an OSI-approved license on github.com or gitlab.com can now use Gitar for free, with the full Pro feature set and no seat limits. Apply from the [plans page](https://docs.gitar.ai/account-billing/plans.md#open-source-plan) and we'll review your project.

Open Source plan card on the billing page with monthly PR usage

Connections panel listing GitHub, two GitLab instances, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps

### Custom integrations (MCP)

Custom integrations let you extend Gitar with your own tools. Alongside the built-in integrations, you can register an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, or a set of plain instructions, and Gitar's rules and agents can use it while reviewing pull requests and running automations. Configure the environment variables your server needs, store API tokens as org-scoped secrets that are injected at runtime, and point at a private package registry if your server is published to one. Custom integrations are an Enterprise feature. [Custom Integrations (MCP)](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/custom-integrations.md)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Superseded: instructions-only integrations, environment variables, and private registries have since been removed. A custom integration is now an https MCP server URL. For instructions with no server, use [Repo Skills](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/skills.md).

Add Custom Integration dialog with fields for slug, name, descriptions, agent instructions, MCP server, environment variables, and secrets

### Usability improvements

* Connecting a GitHub organization or GitLab group with thousands of repositories or projects is now a much smoother experience, with a background process that imports them asynchronously.
* The repository list has a filter for repositories that aren't enabled, so it's easier to find ones Gitar isn't watching yet.
* Auto-merge can now be set per repository. Like auto-approve, you can turn it on for one repository and off for another, and a repository override that only changes the on/off switch still inherits your organization's merge method.
* When branch protection or a repository ruleset rejects Gitar's push, Gitar now explains that on the pull request once, instead of failing silently and retrying.
* Inline threads close themselves. If you ask Gitar for a change in an inline comment and it pushes the fix, the thread is resolved automatically on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.
* Azure DevOps caught up on the rest of the workflow: `gitar unblock`, CI failure analysis and retry for Azure Pipelines, an auto-merge method picker, selecting multiple projects at install and connecting or disconnecting them individually afterward, and an inline banner when your PAT has expired.
* Bitbucket now supports multiple workspaces under one organization, re-reviews on new commits, reads Bitbucket Pipelines logs, handles fork pull requests, and emails and Slacks your admins if the installation goes unhealthy.

### Bug fixes

* Reviews no longer flag code the pull request didn't touch. A stale base reference could pull already-merged commits from the base branch into the diff, which showed up as findings against changes you never made.
* Force-pushing a branch no longer triggers a full re-review of the whole pull request. Gitar now reviews only what changed since its last review.
* The Gitar dashboard comment now posts reliably on GitLab merge requests. It could previously loop forever and never appear, even though inline findings and the summary posted normally.
* Findings are no longer marked resolved unless the fix actually reached the remote, so a pull request can't be approved on the strength of a commit that was never pushed. Conversely, a push that had nothing left to do no longer leaves findings stuck open.
* Reacting with the checkmark emoji to apply a fix now works on newly connected GitLab organizations. The webhook Gitar needs for emoji reactions wasn't being requested at setup.
* CI Fixer no longer reports CI as green when it isn't.
* `gitar unblock` now respects repository-level setting overrides instead of only reading your organization defaults.
* Fixed a Stripe timing bug that could drop a paying organization back to the Free tier immediately after converting from a trial.
* The Rule Catalog header count now matches the totals shown in each category.

## June 26, 2026

### Azure DevOps and Bitbucket support (Beta)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Azure DevOps and Bitbucket support are in **beta**. Expect rough edges as we round out coverage. We'd love your feedback.

Gitar now works with Azure DevOps and Bitbucket repositories. Connect them right from onboarding alongside GitHub and GitLab, and Gitar posts reviews, PR summaries, and dashboard comments and responds to interactive commands on those pull requests. Connected repos and pull requests show the right platform logo throughout the web app (recent activity, settings, and repo lists), with an "Open in Azure DevOps" / "Open in Bitbucket" link.

Connect your repositories onboarding step with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, and Bitbucket

### Faster responses to your activity

Gitar now reacts immediately to the events you care about (PR/MR opens and closes, comments, pushes, accepted fixes, and enabling auto-apply) instead of waiting out a batch delay, so it feels noticeably more responsive. Only bursty machine signals like CI-failure floods and metadata edits are still batched.

### Usability improvements

* Repository search in your settings is faster and more accurate. Results are ranked by relevance so exact and prefix matches surface first, and a new "All organizations" dropdown narrows the list to a single owner when you have repos across multiple organizations.
* Pro orgs now get double the per-seat review budget, so upgrading from Core translates into tangibly more automated reviews before any pause kicks in.
* When you reply to a finding by proposing or comparing an alternative ("what about exit 1 instead?"), Gitar now treats it as a question rather than an instruction to change code. It only applies and commits a change once you explicitly tell it to.
* Add your own notes below Gitar's PR summary and they stay put. The summary is now a self-contained block that Gitar updates in place, so anything you write underneath it, and any edits you make to the rest of the description, is preserved across summary updates.
* Clearer messaging when you hit a limit. Rate-limit replies now tell you roughly how long to wait before retrying, and when Gitar pauses automatic reviews it now explains that you can still run `Gitar review` manually in the meantime.

### Bug fixes

* Auto-merge failures are now surfaced instead of silently claiming the PR is armed. If your platform rejects enabling auto-merge (repo setting off, missing permission, or nothing to wait on), Gitar tells you the actual reason.
* PR summaries no longer mix in unrelated changes pulled from merging main into your branch. Summaries focus only on the PR's own contributions.
* More consistent review verdicts across pushes: Gitar now retains awareness of findings you've already resolved or dismissed when re-reviewing, so a PR no longer flip-flops between Approved and Changes Requested.
* Resolving all open finding threads now correctly dismisses Gitar's blocking review and clears the check, so the PR becomes mergeable the moment you've addressed every finding.
* Auto-approve now re-applies after you push to an already-approved PR. A clean re-review correctly re-approves instead of leaving the PR stuck without approval.
* Allow-listed bots now work independently of other event-filter lists, so adding just Dependabot (including bot names with periods) gets those PRs reviewed. The manual "Start Review" button also works on bot-authored PRs.
* CI failure analysis now persists across dashboard comment reposts instead of vanishing when a new commit refreshes the comment.
* Findings with blob-URL sources now anchor as inline comments on the affected lines instead of appearing only in the summary.

Auto-approve no longer requires explicit criteria to take effect. When the toggle is enabled and no criteria are configured, neither in your org settings nor in a `.gitar/config/approve.md` file, Gitar will approve PRs automatically when all code review issues are resolved.

If you want to restrict which PRs are auto-approved (for example, only docs changes, only small PRs), set custom criteria in your org settings or add a per-repo `approve.md` file. See [Auto-Approve](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-approve.md) for details.

> [!WARNING]
>
> If you previously had auto-approve enabled without criteria, your PRs were **not** being auto-approved. With this change, those PRs **will** now be auto-approved when the code review passes. Review your auto-approve settings if this is not desired.

# Repository Rules

> Create automated workflows using natural language, no code required

## Overview

Repository rules let you define automated workflows using plain markdown files. When conditions are met, Gitar automatically executes actions, with no code required.

> [card] Natural Language
>
> Write rules in plain English, not code

> [card] Git-Native
>
> Rules live in your repo as `.gitar/rules/*.md`

> [card] Integrations
>
> Connect to Jira, Linear, Slack, and more

## Quick Start

**1. Create the Rules Directory**

```bash theme={null}
mkdir -p .gitar/rules
```

**2. Add a Rule File**

Create `.gitar/rules/security-review.md`:

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Security Review"
description: "Require security team review for sensitive changes"
when: "PRs modifying authentication or encryption code"
actions: "Assign security team and add label"
---

# Security Review

When sensitive code is modified:
- Assign @security-team as reviewer
- Add "security-review" label
- Post comment with security checklist
```

**3. Commit and Push**

```bash theme={null}
git add .gitar/rules/
git commit -m "Add security review rule"
git push
```

**4. Open a PR**

Gitar evaluates your rules on every PR. Expand Verification in the dashboard comment to read check results and recorded actions. When none of them apply, the comment says how many were skipped, and `gitar display:verbose` shows why each was skipped.

## Rule Structure

Rules are markdown files with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Rule Name"
description: "Brief summary of what this rule does"
type: check
when: "Condition that triggers the rule"
actions: "What Gitar does when condition is met"
---

# Detailed Instructions

Natural language description of the rule behavior.
Include specific examples, edge cases, or additional context.
```

### Frontmatter Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| - | - |
| `title` | Names the rule in the dashboard. Without one, Gitar uses the heading or filename. |
| `description` | Summarizes the rule. |
| `slug` | Optional custom rule identifier. It does not preserve evaluation history when the file is renamed. |
| `when` | States the condition that triggers the rule. |
| `actions` | Describes what Gitar does when the condition matches. |
| `type` | `check` validates a requirement. `automation` takes an action. Without a type, Gitar infers it from the rule. |

## Triggers

| Event | What Gitar evaluates |
| - | - |
| A PR is opened | Full rule evaluation on all applicable rules |
| New commits are pushed to a PR | Re-evaluates checks, may fire automations |
| CI fails on a PR | CI-related automations, such as retrying unrelated failures |
| PR metadata updates | Title, description, reviewers, or labels change |
| A PR is closed or merged | Post-merge workflows like follow-up issue creation, compliance reporting, and merge-close notifications |

## Supported Actions

> [accordion] Post Comments
>
> Post comments on the PR or as inline code reviews.
>
> ```markdown theme={null}
> actions: "Post a comment summarizing the database schema changes"
> ```

> [accordion] Apply Labels
>
> Add or remove labels based on detected conditions.
>
> ```markdown theme={null}
> actions: "Add 'needs-docs' label if README is modified"
> ```

> [accordion] Assign Reviewers
>
> Assign specific reviewers when changes are detected.
>
> ```markdown theme={null}
> actions: "Assign @backend-team for API changes"
> ```

> [accordion] Suggest Code Changes
>
> Suggest or make code modifications.
>
> ```markdown theme={null}
> actions: "Suggest adding error handling for new API endpoints"
> ```

## Integrations

Every integration your organization has enabled is available to every rule. Name one in the rule and the agent uses it, so `post to #releases` finds Slack and `move the ticket to In Review` finds Linear.

| Integration | Example action | Setup |
| - | - | - |
| Jira | Link the PR to a ticket and update its status. | [Jira](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/jira.md) |
| Linear | Move a linked issue to In Review. | [Linear](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/linear.md) |
| Plane | Open a follow-up work item. | [Plane](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/plane.md) |
| YouTrack | Comment on the linked issue. | [YouTrack](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/youtrack.md) |
| Slack | Post a merge notification to a channel. | [Slack](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/slack.md) |

### Custom Integrations (MCP)

On the Enterprise plan you can connect your own MCP servers as custom integrations. Name one in a rule the same way you name a built-in.

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Internal Docs Enrichment"
when: "PRs that modify a documented internal service"
actions: "Comment with links to the relevant internal docs"
---

When a PR touches a documented service, use the Acme Search integration to
find the relevant internal docs and link them in a review comment.
```

See [Custom Integrations](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/custom-integrations.md) for setup instructions.

### Skills

A rule can also call a skill, a procedure committed under `.gitar/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Name it in the rule body and the agent loads it and follows it.

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Migration Safety"
when: "PRs that add or modify files under db/migrations/"
actions: "Comment with any reversibility or ordering problems"
---

When a PR touches `db/migrations/`, use the `migration-check` skill and post
its findings as a review comment.
```

Naming the skill is what invokes it. Gitar has no slash-command syntax. See [Skills](https://docs.gitar.ai/integrations/skills.md) for the file format.

To call the same skill from rules in every repository, commit it once to your [configuration repository](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/configuration-repository.md).

## Rules for Every Repository

A rule in `.gitar/rules/` applies to the repository that holds it. To apply one across the organization, commit it to your [configuration repository](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/configuration-repository.md) instead and every repository evaluates it.

A repository overrides an inherited rule with a file of the same name, ignoring case and treating `-` and `_` alike. Commit `.gitar/rules/no-raw-sql.md` and the configuration repository's `no-raw-sql.md` (or `no_raw_sql.md`) is skipped for that repository.

## Example Rules

Each example below is one complete `.gitar/rules/*.md` file.

### Documentation Required

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Documentation Required"
description: "Require documentation updates alongside API changes"
when: "PRs adding or modifying API endpoints"
actions: "Request documentation update if not included"
---

# Documentation Requirements

When API endpoints are added or modified:
1. Check if corresponding docs are updated
2. If not, add "needs-docs" label
3. Post comment requesting documentation
```

### Breaking Change Review

```markdown theme={null}
---
title: "Breaking Change Review"
description: "Flag PRs with breaking changes for extra review"
when: "PRs with breaking changes to public APIs"
actions: "Add breaking-change label and request senior review"
---

# Breaking Change Detection

Detect breaking changes:
- Removed public methods or fields
- Changed method signatures
- Modified API response schemas

When detected:
- Add "breaking-change" label
- Assign @api-owners as reviewers
- Post checklist for migration guide
```

For dependency updates that should merge automatically, configure [Auto-Approve](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-approve.md) and [Auto-Merge](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-merge.md) criteria.

## Debugging

Use display mode commands to see how rules are being evaluated:

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `gitar display:verbose` | Show full rule evidence and skipped-rule reasons in Verification |
| `gitar display:compact` | Show bounded successful names and all unmet checks (default) |

Verbose Verification showing rule evidence and skipped-rule reasons

## Best Practices

Keep each rule focused on one outcome. Name specific paths and conditions, and include the exceptions that matter to the team. Use `gitar display:verbose` to check why a rule matched or was skipped.

# Organization Settings

> Customize Gitar's Behavior

Open **Settings -> Configuration** in the dashboard to customize how Gitar operates across your organization. Behavior controls sit in the **Behavior** card.

## Configuration Scopes

Settings are configured at two levels:

* **Organization level**: sets the defaults for every repository connected to Gitar.
* **Repository level**: overrides specific org defaults for a single repo.

The org view is where you set defaults for behavior controls such as skip draft PRs, merge blocking, auto-approve, and auto-merge. When a repository needs different behavior, open its overrides dialog from the repository list. The dialog highlights which settings differ from the org default and lets you reset any override in one click.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Repository overrides only change settings that are explicitly toggled. Everything else inherits from the org default.

## Behavior

Behavior settings

### Skip drafts

When enabled, Gitar ignores draft PRs until they are marked ready for review.

### Enhance summaries

When enabled, Gitar auto-fills PR descriptions with a summary of the changes.

### Retry unrelated CI failures

Automatically retry CI jobs whose failures are unrelated to the changes in your PR, for example flaky tests or transient infrastructure issues. See [CI retry](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/ci-failure-analysis.md#ci-retry-for-unrelated-failures) for supported platforms and retry limits.

### Block merges

Configure a severity threshold for Gitar's code review verdict. When findings meet or exceed the threshold, Gitar submits a blocking review to prevent merging.

Whether the host enforces that block or only records it differs. See [Platform Support](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/platform-support.md).

### `gitar unblock`

Turn on **Enable the `gitar unblock` command** to let any member dismiss Gitar's blocking review by commenting `gitar unblock`. The toggle appears once **Block merges** is set to a level other than **Never**.

### Auto-approve

Enable **Auto-approve PRs based on code review** to let Gitar submit an approving review when a PR passes code review. You can optionally provide natural-language criteria to restrict which PRs qualify. When no criteria are configured, Gitar approves any PR with no blocking findings.

See [Auto-Approve](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-approve.md) for criteria examples, per-repo config files, and platform behavior.

### `gitar-approved` label

Enable **Apply gitar-approved label** in the auto-approve settings to mark approved PRs. See [`gitar-approved`](https://docs.gitar.ai/labels#gitar-approved) for label behavior.

### Auto-merge

Enable **Auto-merge PRs** to arm your platform's native auto-merge immediately after Gitar approves. The toggle appears once auto-approve is on. On [GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/automatically-merging-a-pull-request) and Azure DevOps you can choose the merge method (squash, merge commit, or rebase). On [GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/auto_merge/) the project's default merge method is used.

Two more controls sit under the toggle.

**Auto-merge criteria** takes your merge conditions in plain language, evaluated in the same pass as auto-approve.

**Require `.gitar/config/merge.md`** holds every repository back until it commits its own criteria file, so only repositories that opt in are armed.

Availability differs by host. See [Platform Support](https://docs.gitar.ai/connecting-code/platform-support.md).

See [Auto-Merge](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-merge.md) for prerequisites and details.

### Auto-apply review criteria

Use the **Auto-apply review criteria** card to limit which review findings Gitar may fix automatically. Saving criteria does not enable automatic fixes on a PR. See [Auto-Apply](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/auto-apply.md) for per-PR controls and repository criteria.

### Functional validation

Enable **Validate PRs against linked issues** to have Gitar read the issues a PR links, split each into objectives, and judge the diff against them. On by default where it is available, and set for the whole organization. See [Functional Validation](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/functional-validation.md).

### Review depth

Enterprise organization admins can choose **Thorough** to include smaller verified issues or **Focused** to prioritize higher-impact findings. Set the organization default here, then select **Customize** on a repository to override it. Reset an override to inherit the default. See [Code Review](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review.md#review-depth).

## Custom Instructions

Provide organization-wide instructions that guide the Gitar agent across all connected repositories. These are applied to every repo in your org. Use them to enforce coding standards, preferred libraries, or architectural patterns.

Gitar also reads instruction files committed to each repository. See [Repository Customization](https://docs.gitar.ai/configuration/repository-config.md) for which files and where they go.

Custom instructions

### Review summary instructions

Gitar writes a short summary under the **Code Review** header on every PR. Add instructions here to say how that summary should read.

Set length, structure, register, tone, or the language it is written in. Leave the field empty and you get the default: one or two sentences.

For example:

```text theme={null}
Write three or four sentences, no bullets. Open with the service the change
touches, then the most severe finding. Use plain past tense and never address
the author as "you".
```

### Risk classification and instructions

**Risk classification** assesses whole-PR risk and shows labels in reviews and the dashboard. Organization admins can turn it off or refine the default levels with **Risk instructions**.

Repositories can add policy in `.gitar/config/risk.md`. See [Risk Triage](https://docs.gitar.ai/features/code-review/risk-triage.md) for level definitions and how policy affects approval and merge criteria.

## Scope

Control which PRs Gitar processes, by author or by the branch a PR merges into. Every field is a comma-separated list, no spaces, and is set for the whole organization rather than per repository.

Scope settings

| Field | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Allowed authors** | Only process PRs from these users. Leave empty to process all users |
| **Excluded authors** | Skip PRs from these users, even if they match the allowed list |
| **Allowed bots** | Bot accounts Gitar should process. By default all bot-authored changes are skipped. Add bots like Dependabot or Renovate here to include them |
| **Allowed target branches** | Only process PRs merging *into* a matching branch. Leave empty to process every target branch |
| **Excluded target branches** | Never process PRs merging into a matching branch. Takes precedence over the allowed list |

### Target branch patterns

Branch fields take names or shell globs: `main`, `release/*`, `*-staging`. Matching is case-insensitive and `*` spans `/`, so `feature/*` also matches `feature/a/b`. Full refs like `refs/heads/main` are accepted and normalized.

Put `main,master,release/*` in the allowed list to keep Gitar off stacked and sandbox branches. Put `feature/*,sandbox/*` in the excluded list to drop a few destinations and leave the rest on.

The filter runs when Gitar first picks up a PR and again on automatic push-triggered reviews. Retargeting into an excluded branch stops the next automatic review. Manually started reviews can still run.

### Skipping PRs with `gitar-skip`

Use [`gitar-skip`](https://docs.gitar.ai/labels#gitar-skip) to skip automatic processing for an individual PR. See [Labels](https://docs.gitar.ai/labels.md) for all supported labels and how they interact.

# Reviewing this repository

This repository is a CSCI 435 course fork of Gitea. Pull requests are graded against the course
rules as well as Gitea's own conventions, so review against both. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are
read already; these are the course and project rules they point to:

@.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md
@.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md
@CONTRIBUTING.md
@docs/sprint0/standards.md

## Focus on

- Whether the change does what the linked issue's acceptance criteria ask, and nothing outside its
  scope.
- Whether each test checks real behaviour and can fail: no assertion that passes for an unrelated
  reason, no "nothing happened" check without waiting, no test that depends on fixture data by
  chance.
- Bugs and security problems, with the input or state that triggers them.

## Leave alone

- The pull request description's sections and format: CodeRabbit checks those.
- The pull request title's Conventional Commit format: the `pr-title` CI job checks it.
- Formatting and anything else the repository's linters already enforce (`make lint`).
- Style preferences that no rule above asks for. These are students learning a large codebase;
  one clear finding helps more than several small ones.

# Skipped tests and disabled checks

The course and `AGENTS.md` say: never skip a test or disable a CI check without a linked issue and
a code comment giving the reason.

Count only what this pull request adds or changes:

- Go: `t.Skip`, `t.Skipf`, `t.SkipNow`.
- Vitest and Playwright: `test.skip`, `it.skip`, `describe.skip`, `test.fixme`, `test.fail`, and
  the same through `.skipIf` or `.runIf`.
- Workflows under `.github/workflows/`: a job or step that runs tests or a check and is turned off
  (`if: false`), removed, or allowed to fail (`continue-on-error: true`).

Each one is met when a comment next to it gives the reason and names an issue (`#123` or a link to
it). Skips that already existed and that the pull request does not touch are not counted.

# Commit messages

From `AGENTS.md`. Check every commit in the pull request except merge commits (subjects starting
with `Merge`).

1. The subject is a Conventional Commit, `type(scope): subject`, with `!` before the colon for a
   breaking change. A commit that only changes tests uses the `test` type.
2. When the pull request closes an issue (`Closes #123`), the subject ends with that issue's number,
   for example `(#123)`. Chore pull requests that close no issue are exempt.
3. AI help is credited with a trailer in the form `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION`, for
   example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`, never with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer that
   names an AI tool or model.

A `Signed-off-by:` trailer is not judged: signing off is the human author's own step.

# Expected values in tests

The course's Test Evidence rule (`.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`): an expected value comes
from the acceptance criteria, the issue discussion, docs or upstream behaviour, never from the
current output of the code under test. A test that copies the code's output cannot catch the code
being wrong.

For each assertion the pull request adds or changes (`assert`/`require` in Go, `expect` in Vitest
and Playwright), find the matching row of the description's "Test Evidence" table and its "Source of
expected value". The value is met when it appears in, or follows directly from, that source: the
linked issue's acceptance criteria or discussion, quoted docs, or the behaviour the row says it
keeps.

Flag only clear cases:

- a value that the cited source does not contain and the row does not explain under "other";
- a snapshot or golden file that was regenerated with no source given;
- a value that only repeats a constant or string from the code under test.

Setup values such as fixture IDs, user names and timeouts are not expected values.

<!-- Title (reference only, don't paste this line): chore(gitar): add course review instructions and three checks -->

## What changed and Why

Gitar reviews every pull request here with its default settings: its verification shows "Rules: No rules evaluated", and it approves any pull request it finds no blocking problem in, although the course only counts a teammate's approval. This PR gives it the course's rules to review against, and three checks for graded rules that nothing checks today. Per Gitar's docs, it already reads `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` from the repository root, so those aren't repeated.

- **`.gitar/review/course.md`** tells Gitar this is a course fork, pulls in the course and project rules (`.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, `.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/sprint0/standards.md`), and asks it to focus on acceptance criteria, tests that can fail, and real bugs. It leaves the PR description's format to CodeRabbit, the PR title to the `pr-title` CI job, and formatting to the linters, so the bots don't repeat each other.
- **`.gitar/rules/skipped-tests-need-an-issue.md`**: a skipped or expected-to-fail test, or a turned-off CI check, added by the PR needs a linked issue and a reason in a code comment (a Sprint 3 rule and an `AGENTS.md` rule).
- **`.gitar/rules/commit-messages.md`**: each commit is a Conventional Commit, ends with the issue number when the PR closes an issue, and credits AI with an `Assisted-by:` trailer rather than `Co-Authored-By:` (`AGENTS.md`). The `pr-title` job only checks the title, not the commits.
- **`.gitar/rules/test-expected-values.md`**: each expected value in a new or changed test can be traced to the source its Test Evidence row cites, not to the code's own output (the course's Test Evidence rule, worth 6 of a PR's 20 D4 points).

## Before merging (needs the Gitar admin)

Turn off auto-approval: in Gitar's settings, Configuration → Behavior → **Auto-approve PRs based on code review**. A file can't do this: Gitar only reads approval criteria, not an off switch, from the repository. Gitar's docs don't say whether the OSS plan has this setting; if it doesn't, a one-line `.gitar/config/approve.md` asking it never to approve is the fallback, though that is only an instruction to the bot.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N/A: review-bot configuration only, no product behaviour changes | N/A | N/A | N/A |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** N/A

**AI-written tests:** None.

## CI / manual verification

- The four files pass markdownlint, `make lint-spell` and `make lint-editorconfig`, with no trailing whitespace.
- Each rule uses the layout from Gitar's rules documentation (`title`, `description`, `type: check`, `when`, `actions`, then the details).
- Every file the review instructions pull in exists, and the `pr-title` job they mention is in `.github/workflows/pull-labeler.yml`.
- Not verified: how Gitar applies them. Its docs don't say whether `.gitar/review/` and `.gitar/rules/` are read from `main` or from the PR's branch, so this PR may not be reviewed with them; the first PR after it merges will be. Rules then show in Gitar's Verification section as "Rules n/3 met".

## Design

- Gitar gets review instructions plus checks for rules nothing else checks, rather than copies of CodeRabbit's checks, so each graded rule has one bot looking at it.
- Three checks: two clear-cut ones (skipped tests, commit messages) and one that targets the most points but is the hardest for a bot to judge (expected values); that one is written to flag only clear cases, and can be deleted if it proves noisy.
- Approval is turned off by the admin rather than by a file, because no file can turn it off.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- None.

**Encountered:**
- Gitar's docs leave open which branch the review and rule files are read from, and whether the OSS plan can turn auto-approval off; both are noted above rather than guessed.

## AI assistance

Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) from the decisions I made (review instructions plus three checks, no auto-approval), after it read Gitar's documentation, and checked against the repository's linters. Verified by me, and every commit was made by me.
